sources.name: Climate Change Knowledge Portal (CCKP): ERA5 and CMIP6 aggregated to countries, ADM1 and watersheds
sources.publisher: World Bank Group
sources.measures: Observed climate (ERA5 0.25°, CRU 0.5°) and CMIP6 projections (0.25°, by SSP), aggregated to country (ADM0), first-level subnational (ADM1), watershed, EEZ. Variables include tas/tasmax/tasmin (°C), precipitation, hd35 (days with Tmax >35°C), frost days and others. Values are absolute or anomalies by period.
sources.coverage: Global. Every country and ADM1 unit uses World Bank Official Boundaries codes (e.g. IND, USA.2593214). ERA5 annual time series 1950–2025 (verified to 2025). CMIP6 climatologies cover 1995–2014 and 20-year windows to 2100.
sources.latest_release: The ERA5 annual country series includes 2025 (the period code 1950-2025 returned 76 values on 2026-10-04). The portal has no visible version or date stamp, so the exact refresh date is unverified.
sources.update_cadence: About annual for the ERA5 series. CMIP6 projections are static.
sources.format: REST JSON (or _format=xlsx). The UI also offers bulk 'global_countries_subnationals' downloads.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 plus the World Bank Dataset Terms (https://www.worldbank.org/en/about/legal/terms-of-use-for-datasets). Quoted from the CCKP Terms tab: 'Unless specifically labeled otherwise, these Datasets are provided to you under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0), with the additional terms below' (a mediation/arbitration clause). Attribution format: 'The World Bank: Dataset name: Data source (if known)'. You may not imply World Bank endorsement.
sources.citation: The World Bank: Climate Change Knowledge Portal (CCKP), [collection e.g. ERA5 0.25° timeseries, tas, annual 1950–2025, country aggregation]: Copernicus Climate Change Service ERA5 (Hersbach et al. 2023, doi:10.24381/cds.f17050d7) / CMIP6 multi-model ensemble. https://climateknowledgeportal.worldbank.org
sources.doi: None found for CCKP itself. Cite the upstream ERA5 DOI, 10.24381/cds.f17050d7.
sources.status: Active. The API answered on 2026-10-04. The website returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients (bot protection) but opened in a real browser.
sources.url_check: curl and WebFetch on climateknowledgeportal.worldbank.org returned 403. The Browser pane loaded the download-data page and showed the 'Terms of Use' tab text (CC BY 4.0 quoted above) and the 'API Structure' tab (template GET https://cckpapi.worldbank.org/cckp/v1/{collection}_{type}_{variable}_{product}_{aggregation}_{period}_{percentile}_{scenario}_{model}_{calc}_{statistic}/{geocode}). The API call era5...1950-2025.../IND returned {"status":"success"} with values '2024-07':24.77, '2025-07':24.27. The CMIP6 hd35 call returned IND 1995-2014=77.88 days and 2040-2059 SSP2-4.5=94.78 days.
sources.site_use: Primary engine for 'how has MY country/state warmed' and 'what's coming'. Show a country (and ADM1) annual temperature line from 1950 to the latest year, with the 1951–1980 mean as a reference band, and a 'hot days >35°C now vs 2050' card by SSP. Because it shares World Bank Official Boundaries codes, the map polygons and numbers line up exactly.
sources.caveats: These are reanalysis (ERA5) aggregates, not station records. Aggregation is land-area-weighted within World Bank boundaries, which are disputed in places. Absolute °C values are returned, so the site must compute anomalies itself and publish the baseline years. Per-model spread is hidden by the 'median' percentile, so show p10–p90 for projections. There is no published version string, so snapshot the JSON with its fetch date in the provenance record.

sources.name: ERA5 monthly averaged data on single levels (Copernicus C3S), plus the OWID country-aggregated temperature anomalies derived from it
sources.publisher: Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) / ECMWF. Aggregator: Our World in Data (OWID).
sources.measures: Global 0.25° reanalysis of 2 m temperature and other variables, monthly means. OWID's derivative gives monthly and annual country temperature anomalies (°C) vs the 1991–2020 mean, latitude-weighted over each country's land area within World Bank boundaries.
sources.coverage: 1940 to Aug 2026 (CDS temporal extent ends 2026-08-01). OWID series: 1940–2025 annual, monthly to latest, about 200 countries plus World.
sources.latest_release: CDS record updated 2026-09-06 (STAC 'updated'). OWID indicator lastUpdated 2026-09-11, origin datePublished 2026-08-21.
sources.update_cadence: Monthly (ERA5T preliminary, finalised about 2–3 months later). OWID refreshes monthly.
sources.format: ERA5: NetCDF/GRIB via the CDS API (free ECMWF account and licence acceptance needed to download). OWID: CSV plus JSON metadata.
sources.license: ERA5: CC BY 4.0 (the CDS STAC license link is https://spdx.org/licenses/CC-BY-4.0, titled 'CC-BY licence'). OWID-produced data is CC BY 4.0 ('All visualizations, data, and code produced by Our World in Data are completely open access under the Creative Commons BY license'). The OWID citation must carry 'Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information'.
sources.citation: Hersbach, H., Bell, B., Berrisford, P., et al. (2023): ERA5 monthly averaged data on single levels from 1940 to present. Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) Climate Data Store (CDS), DOI: 10.24381/cds.f17050d7 (Accessed on <date>). For OWID: 'Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information (2026) – with major processing by Our World in Data. “Temperature anomaly” [dataset]'.
sources.url_check: Fetched the CDS STAC JSON: title 'ERA5 monthly averaged data on single levels from 1940 to present', updated 2026-09-06T00:00:00Z, temporal interval 1940-01-01 to 2026-08-01, license link spdx CC-BY-4.0, sci:doi 10.24381/cds.f17050d7. Fetched the OWID CSV (header 'entity,code,year,temperature_anomaly'; World 2024=0.7195, 2025=0.5916; Germany 2024=1.5575). OWID metadata says 'major processing', with lastUpdated 2026-09-11.
sources.site_use: Upstream of record for country temperature. Use the OWID annual country anomaly CSV as a fast, clean cross-check of the CCKP series and for 'this month vs normal' country tiles. Always show the baseline (1991–2020) next to the number.
sources.caveats: OWID applies 'major processing' (its own boundary clipping, latitude weighting and 1991–2020 baseline), so the values are OWID-derived, not Copernicus-published. They also differ from CCKP's ERA5 aggregation and from national met-office series. OWID notes the method may be unreliable for very small countries. The 1991–2020 baseline already contains about 0.9°C of warming, so anomalies look smaller than vs pre-industrial or 1951–1980. Explain this, or re-baseline from CCKP absolutes.

sources.latest_release: Page updated 2026-09-11. Gridded file gistemp1200_GHCNv4_ERSSTv5.nc.gz Last-Modified 2026-09-08.
sources.format: CSV, NetCDF, Zarr, SBBX
sources.license: NASA Earth science data guidance (earthdata.nasa.gov data-use-guidance): 'data provided from a NASA-led mission are licensed as Creative Commons Zero (CC0)'. Users are 'very strongly urged to cite the data'. The GISTEMP page has no separate data licence (graphics follow NASA media guidelines).
sources.citation: GISTEMP Team, 2026: GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP), version 4. NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies. Dataset accessed <date> at https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/. Lenssen, N., et al. (2024), J. Geophys. Res. Atmos., 129(17), e2023JD040179, doi:10.1029/2023JD040179.
sources.status: At-risk but still updating. Wikipedia (GISS article) records NASA terminating the Armstrong Hall lease on 25 Apr 2025 and GISS staff working remotely from 1 Jun 2025. The GISTEMP page itself shows no discontinuation notice and was updated 2026-09-11.
sources.url_check: Fetched the landing page (updated 11 Sep 2026, citation text). Fetched GLB.Ts+dSST.csv: the 2025 row has J-D=1.19, and the 2026 row runs through Aug (1.40). A HEAD on the .nc.gz returned 200 with Last-Modified 2026-09-08. Fetched the NASA Earthdata data-use-guidance page (CC0 statement).
sources.site_use: Secondary cross-check for the global number shown above every country drill-down, and an independent dataset beside ERA5. The 250 km grid can be clipped to countries only if the site documents its own aggregation. Prefer CCKP for country series.
sources.caveats: There is no official country series, so any country number would be the site's own derivation. Its baseline (1951–1980) differs from ERA5/OWID (1991–2020). Mirror the files, because federal continuity is uncertain.

sources.coverage: 1850/1750 to recent. Global and regional gridded files are public. Country, state and city series are 'available by request only'.
sources.latest_release: High-resolution dataset still labelled 'PRELIMINARY DATA – SUBJECT TO CHANGE'. The sample Malaysia file says 'This analysis was run on 06-Mar-2023'. The data page mentions a description paper open for review (2 Sep 2026). The legacy public country files (berkeley-earth-temperature.s3.us-west-1) come from an 08-Jun-2016 run (file Last-Modified 2023-10-26).
sources.update_cadence: Irregular for national series (on request). Monthly for global.
sources.format: Plain text, NetCDF
sources.license: Quoted from the data page: 'Berkeley Earth's data is licensed under Creative Commons BY-NC 4.0 International for non-commercial use only.' Commercial licensing goes via admin@berkeleyearth.org. https://berkeleyearth.org/data-license/ returned 404.
sources.citation: Berkeley Earth, www.berkeleyearth.org (the page asks to reference Berkeley Earth and the URL). No dataset DOI was shown on the page.
sources.doi: None shown on the data page (not verified)
sources.status: Active organisation. National series are gated behind a request form, and the public country files are stale (2016 run).
sources.url_check: Fetched the data page (license quote, 'available by request only', request-form links). The license page returned 404. Read the Malaysia sample header ('PRELIMINARY DATA … NOT YET PEER REVIEWED', analysis run 06-Mar-2023, baseline Jan 1951–Dec 1980). The legacy US file header says 'analysis was run on 08-Jun-2016'.
sources.site_use: Do not use for headline numbers. At most, cite it as a methodological cross-reference in 'how we know' notes.
sources.caveats: Fails the traceability goal: activists cannot download the same country file without a request form, the data is preliminary, and the files are NC-licensed. The legacy public country files have not been rerun since 2016.

sources.license: No explicit licence found. The download page shows only a 'Suggested Citation' and 'Copyright © 2026'. The About page calls the tools 'free and open-access'. The codebook PDF contains no licence text. An optional one-minute questionnaire is requested, with no registration.
sources.citation: Notre Dame Global Adaptation Initiative Country Index (ND-GAIN). (2026). University of Notre Dame.
sources.url_check: Fetched the download page (one zip link, suggested citation). The zip returned HTTP 403 to curl's default UA and 200 (4,910,250 bytes, application/zip) with a browser UA. Listed the archive and read gain/gain.csv (header ISO3, Name, 1995…2024). 2024 values: NOR 71.85, FIN 71.10, DEU 69.23 … TCD 26.42, SOM 27.00, ERI 27.36. The About page and codebook had no licence text.

sources.format: XLSX (zipped), NetCDF/TXT gridmaps
sources.license: Mixed. Booklet 'Conditions of use': 'Unless otherwise noted, all material owned by the European Union is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence.' But 'IEA-EDGAR CO2 (v5) data are … licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Users of IEA-EDGAR CO2 data should contact the IEA at compliance@iea.org for permission to use.' 'Users of the data are obliged to acknowledge the source … with reference to the EDGAR report webpage … and EDGAR_2026_GHG website.' The 1 km folder copyright.txt says CC BY 4.0.

Parsed the booklet xlsx in memory. Sheets: info, Citations and references, GHG_totals_by_country, GHG_by_sector_and_country, GHG_per_GDP_by_country, GHG_per_capita_by_country, LULUCF_*. GLOBAL TOTAL 2024=53,769.6 and 2025=54,149.2 Mt CO2eq. USA per-capita 2025=17.53, IND=3.11, CHN=11.11, global 6.62 t.
sources.site_use: Main source for national GHG totals, sector stacks and per-capita all-gas comparisons, 1970–2025. The 0.1°/1 km grids power 'where in my country' heatmaps. The CH4/N2O/F-gas files can be redistributed freely under CC BY.
sources.caveats: Because the fossil-CO2 component (the biggest one) is CC BY-NC-ND, publishing modified CSVs (per-capita, re-aggregated sectors, any total that includes fossil CO2) arguably breaches 'no derivatives'. Before offering derived CSVs, email compliance@iea.org for permission, or show EDGAR's own published per-capita and total columns verbatim and link to the booklet. The site's non-commercial status helps with NC but not with ND. Uses GWP-100 AR5 and excludes LULUCF in its totals. EDGAR country codes include pseudo-entities (AIR, SEA, 'GLOBAL TOTAL', EU27).

Also includes 'top emission reduction strategies'.

sources.license: Terms page (climatetrace.org/terms): CC BY 4.0, 'anyone is free to copy, modify and distribute Climate TRACE data in any format for any purpose, including commercial use, as long as you attribute it to Climate TRACE and indicate if you have made any changes'. The terms also warn that some external datasets included may carry different licences.
sources.citation: Climate TRACE – Tracking Real-time Atmospheric Carbon Emissions (2026). Climate TRACE Emissions Inventory, release 5.11.0 (24 Sep 2026). https://climatetrace.org [accessed <date>]. Exact suggested wording is in the Climate TRACE data guide and methodology repository (github.com/climatetracecoalition/methodology-documents); the guide was not fetched.
sources.status: Active. The API is labelled 'Public API (Beta)'.
sources.url_check: Fetched the data page (release 5.11.0, 24 Sep 2026; API https://api.climatetrace.org/v7) and the terms page (CC BY 4.0 quote). openapi.json title 'Climate TRACE API' version 7.2.0, with paths /v7/admins, /v7/cities, /v7/rankings/countries, /v7/sources/emissions (params year, gas, sectors, gadmId, cityId…). Live results: global 2025 co2e_100yr = 54,418,388,107 t. China 16.60 Gt (11.77 t/cap). USA 6.35 Gt (19.16 t/cap). California State (USA.5_1) 435.8 Mt. Wyoming State 114.3 Mt. London Urban Area (ghs-fua_5288) 67.6 Mt. The legacy v6 /country/emissions endpoint gave a different world total (57.79 Gt for 2025).
sources.site_use: Main subnational and city layer outside the US/UK/EU: state → city → the top 10 named facilities emitting in that place. This is the most 'actionable' view (who owns the emitting assets). The monthly series gives near-real-time 'this year so far'.
sources.caveats: Admin areas use GADM IDs. GADM's licence says 'Redistribution or commercial use is not allowed without prior permission', so do NOT redistribute GADM/Climate TRACE admin polygons. Join IDs to World Bank or Natural Earth geometries instead. Estimates are model-based (satellite plus AI) and can differ widely from official inventories (e.g. Wyoming 114 Mt CO2e all-gas vs EIA 50 Mt energy-CO2). Always label scope. API v6 and v7 totals differ, so pin the API version and release number in provenance. The data is revised every release.

drilldown_paths: World → country (cause view): globe choropleth of per-capita GHG (EDGAR 2026 GHG_per_capita_by_country) → click a country → 1970–2025 total and sector stack (EDGAR booklet GHG_by_sector_and_country) → 'who emitted first' cumulative share bar (OWID co2-data share_global_cumulative_co2, GCB 2025) → production vs consumption gap (OWID consumption_co2_per_capita). Denominators from WDI SP.POP.TOTL. Country polygons from Natural Earth or World Bank Official Boundaries.

Country → consequences: annual temperature since 1950 with the 1951–1980 band (CCKP era5-x0.25 tas timeseries) → 'this year vs normal' (OWID ERA5 anomaly vs 1991–2020, labelled) → 'hot days now vs 2050' under SSP1-2.6/2-4.5/5-8.5 (CCKP cmip6 hd35 climatologies) → people exposed (GHS-POP R2023A zonal sum over CCKP grid or ADM1) → vulnerability vs readiness (ND-GAIN gain/vulnerability/readiness CSVs).

Country → state/province (both sides): ADM1 choropleth. US: EIA SEDS per-capita CO2 by state → fuel/sector history 1960–2024 → NOAA Climate at a Glance state and county temperature 1895–2025. UK: DESNZ local authority → sector/sub-sector → 'within LA scope of influence'. EU: Eurostat env_air_gge country → CRF sector, plus EDGAR 1 km grid for the regional heatmap. Rest of world: Climate TRACE v7 /sources/emissions?gadmId (ADM1/2, IDs crosswalked to World Bank geometry) plus CCKP ADM1 temperature.

State → city → facility: urban centre from GHS-UCDB R2024A (population, heat exposure, EDGAR-derived emissions themes) → Climate TRACE cityId=ghs-fua_* total and monthly trend through Jul 2026 → top named emitting sources and owners in that city (Climate TRACE /v7/sources ranked) → what the city has pledged and reported (GCoM MyCovenant 7th release df1/df2/df3; CDP-ICLEI only as an outbound link).

Compare two places side by side (clarity mode): pick any two countries or states → same-scope metrics only (EDGAR all-GHG per capita, OWID cumulative share, CCKP warming 2016–2025 vs 1951–1980, ND-GAIN). Every number carries a scope chip ('energy CO2 only', 'all GHG excl. LULUCF', 'model estimate', 'officially reported').

'Official vs independent' lens for any country: Eurostat/EEA (EU), DESNZ (UK), EPA state inventory (US, to 2022), PRIMAP-hist HISTCR (Global South; NC-SA) vs EDGAR and Climate TRACE. The divergence (e.g. Wyoming 50 Mt EIA energy-CO2 vs 114 Mt Climate TRACE all-gas) becomes a teaching moment about scope.

Provenance drill (for every number): click any figure → panel with source name, publisher, vintage/release date, exact file URL or API call, row/column used, transformation formula, licence, and a link to the site's frozen snapshot of the raw file (where the licence allows redistribution).
research.action_links:
How the data connects to action (only verified sources):
(1) Individuals: compare personal context to the country and world per-capita averages (EDGAR 2026 per-capita sheet; OWID consumption-based CO2 per capita). The sector stack shows where national emissions come from (EDGAR GHG_by_sector_and_country: power, transport, buildings, agriculture), so a visitor can see which everyday systems dominate. Do not invent a personal 'budget' number without a cited source.
(2) Communities and cities: the DESNZ column 'Emissions within the scope of influence of LAs (kt CO2)' shows what a UK council can actually change. The GCoM MyCovenant 7th release (JRC, CC BY 4.0) lists, for 12,312 signatory cities, their 2020/2030/2050 commitments (commitment_CoM2030_flag etc.), action plans (df2) and monitoring progress (df3). Visitors can check whether their city signed and whether it reports progress. Climate TRACE names the largest emitting facilities and owners in a city or state (/v7/sources ranked; owners via /v7/owners), and its data page offers a 'Top Emission Reduction Strategies' dataset, giving activists concrete targets for local advocacy.
(3) Policymakers and advocates: official vs independent inventories (Eurostat/EEA, DESNZ, EIA vs EDGAR/Climate TRACE) show progress against 1990/2005 baselines (EU −38% vs 1990; UK local authorities −46% vs 2005). ND-GAIN readiness vs vulnerability shows where adaptation finance matters most (Chad 26.4 vs Norway 71.8). CCKP CMIP6 scenarios (SSP1-2.6 vs SSP5-8.5) let users see how much of the future heat (e.g. days >35°C) depends on emissions choices. Climate Watch (WRI; CC BY 4.0, verified at climatewatchdata.org/about/permissions; citation 'Climate Watch. 2026. Washington, DC: World Resources Institute') provides NDC targets and net-zero pledges per country for a 'what has my government promised' link. Note its FAO-sourced LULUCF data requires FAO permission to republish.
Sources: https://edgar.jrc.ec.europa.eu/report_2026 ; https://github.com/owid/co2-data ; https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/uk-local-authority-and-regional-greenhouse-gas-emissions-statistics-2005-to-2024 ; https://data.europa.eu/data/datasets/6684edc9-9b78-464a-990d-810555957550 ; https://climatetrace.org/data ; https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/env_air_gge/default/table ; https://gain.nd.edu/our-work/country-index/download-data/ ; https://climateknowledgeportal.worldbank.org/download-data ; https://www.climatewatchdata.org/about/permissions
research.gaps_and_risks:
LICENCE TRAPS (most important for the 'every number traceable and downloadable' promise):
(a) EDGAR's fossil-CO2 component (IEA-EDGAR CO2 v5) is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The site is non-commercial, but 'no derivatives' means re-aggregated or per-capita CSVs that include fossil CO2 are risky. Either show EDGAR's own published columns verbatim and link to the official xlsx, or get written permission from compliance@iea.org. EDGAR CH4/N2O/F-gases and the 1 km grids are CC BY 4.0.
(b) PRIMAP-hist switched to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 at v2.8 (2026-09-29). Share-alike would force any derived CSV to be NC-SA, so keep its data separate. v2.7 (CC BY) is the last fully open pin.
(c) Berkeley Earth is CC BY-NC 4.0, and its country series are request-only and preliminary, so avoid it.
(d) The CDP open-data licence is non-commercial, custom, 'all rights reserved', and requires the notice to be kept, so link out only.
(e) Climate TRACE admin IDs are GADM. GADM says 'Redistribution or commercial use is not allowed without prior permission'. Never ship GADM polygons; crosswalk IDs to World Bank Official Boundaries or Natural Earth.
(f) geoBoundaries is not uniformly CC BY: 84 of 230 ADM0 boundaries are ODbL and 10 are CC BY-SA 2.0. Check per boundary.
(g) ND-GAIN publishes no licence (only a suggested citation). Ask for permission before offering re-downloads.
(h) UN M49 sits under the restrictive generic UN website ToU. Store only the factual code mapping, with citation.
(i) Eurostat bars commercial reuse of non-European country data (fine for a non-commercial site, but record it).

STATUS RISKS (mirror raw files on every build, with SHA-256 and fetch date):
- EPA state inventory frozen at 1990–2022 (Sept 2024). The national 1990–2023 report was never finalised on EPA's site. On 12 Sep 2025 EPA proposed removing GHGRP obligations for 46 source categories.
- NASA GISS lost its building (lease terminated 25 Apr 2025, staff remote since Jun 2025). GISTEMP still updates monthly (Sept 2026) but should be treated as at-risk.
- NOAA NCEI Climate at a Glance is live (2025 data present), but sits in the at-risk US federal category. No retirement notice was found.
- UN WPP 2026 is postponed to 11 Jul 2027, so WPP 2024 plus the Togo interim update (19 Jan 2026) stays current.
- geoBoundaries (v6.0.0, Sept 2023) and Natural Earth (v5.1.2, May 2022) are stale but stable.
- Climate TRACE's API is labelled 'Beta': v6 and v7 return different world totals (57.8 vs 54.4 Gt CO2e for 2025), so pin the release (5.11.0) and API version.

COMPARABILITY RISKS (the main threat to 'clarity'):
- Different scopes and gases: EIA energy-CO2 vs EPA/EEA all-GHG vs Climate TRACE model estimates. Wyoming is 50 Mt (EIA, 2024) vs 114 Mt (Climate TRACE, 2025).
- Different GWPs (AR5 vs AR6, 100- vs 20-yr), LULUCF in or out, international bunkers in or out.
- Different temperature baselines: GISTEMP 1951–1980, OWID/ERA5 1991–2020, CCKP absolute values.
- Different population denominators: WDI 8.215 bn vs WPP 8.232 bn for 2025.
- Different entity codes: EDGAR pseudo-codes (GLOBAL TOTAL, EU27, AIR, SEA); OWID_*; GADM; World Bank ADM1CD; ONS E06…; US FIPS/postal.
The site needs a single crosswalk table (ISO3 + M49 + WB + GADM + Natural Earth + national codes) and a 'scope chip' on every number.

COVERAGE GAPS:
- India and China subnational official data is weak. China provincial inventories (CEADs, to 2022) are login-gated with no clear licence. India has no official state GHG inventory.
- The Climate Watch 'UNFCCC Non-Annex I' series is stale (China latest 2014, India 2016 in its API).
- UNFCCC BTR/CRT submissions could not be verified because unfccc.int and di.unfccc.int presented an Imperva CAPTCHA, which was not bypassed. Treat India/China official BTR inventory years as unverified, and use PRIMAP-hist HISTCR (NC-SA) or EDGAR/Climate TRACE with clear labelling.
- Direct GCB national xlsx URLs returned 404 (path changed), so GCB is reached via OWID plus the ESSD DOI. GCB 2026 is expected Nov 2026.
- Copernicus publishes no official country temperature series. Country values are always a derivation (CCKP's or OWID's), so say who did the aggregation.
- CCKP has no version stamp, so snapshot each pull.

ACCESS AND COST:
- CCKP and ND-GAIN block default bot user-agents (403). A build-time fetcher needs a normal UA.
- The ERA5 CDS API needs a free ECMWF account (keep the token in Keychain). The EIA API needs a free key, but bulk xlsx needs none.
- Large files (EEA bundle 2.2 GB, GHS-POP 30ss 461 MB, UCDB 264 MB, EDGAR monthly zips 68–73 MB) must be processed offline into small static JSON/Parquet aggregates. Serve only aggregates plus licence-permitted raw snapshots from object storage, to stay well under $20/month.

verdicts.name: Climate Change Knowledge Portal (CCKP): ERA5 and CMIP6 aggregated to countries, ADM1 and watersheds
verdicts.corrections:
Data, licence and status are confirmed. I re-ran the ERA5 API call: 76 values (1950-07 to 2025-07) for each of the 7 ISO3 codes. A 1950-2026 period code returns an empty data array, so 2025 is the latest year. The hd35 calls return IND 77.88→94.78, NGA 98.49→134.32, USA 11.61→24.15 days. The CCKP site still returns 403 to curl. In a real browser its Terms tab says 'CCKP data is disseminated by the World Bank under its Open Data policy', followed by the CC BY 4.0 Dataset Terms text quoted in the research.

CORRECTION (citation URL): https://www.worldbank.org/en/about/legal/terms-of-use-for-datasets now redirects to the general T&C page (https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/legal/terms-conditions). That page says that for 'the remainder of the Materials, you may make non-commercial uses thereof, but you may not make any derivative work'. An activist following the old link would therefore land on non-commercial terms. Link to the correct page instead: https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/legal/terms-conditions/datasets. It confirms CC BY 4.0 plus the non-binding mediation clause and the attribution format 'The World Bank: Dataset name: Data source (if known)'.

The terms also add a pass-through duty the research left out: 'When sharing or facilitating access to the Datasets, you agree to include the same acknowledgment requirement in any sub-licenses'. Any CSV the site re-serves must carry that requirement.

verdicts.name: Climate TRACE emissions inventory (country, admin-1/2, city and asset level) and API v7
verdicts.corrections:
Confirmed:
- Release 5.11.0 (24 Sep 2026), monthly data to July 2026.
- API v7 (openapi.json actually serves YAML: title 'Climate TRACE API', version 7.2.0, openapi 3.1.0). Paths include /v7/admins, /v7/cities, /v7/owners, /v7/rankings/countries, /v7/sources, /v7/sources/emissions, and /v7/definitions/*.
- Terms are CC BY 4.0, with a warning that some external sources (EDGAR, FAOSTAT, US EPA, EU registers) 'may have different specific terms'.
- The 'Top Emission Reduction Strategies' dataset exists.
- Live values match: global 2025 = 54,418,388,107 t, CHN 16.60 Gt (11.77 t/cap), USA 6.35 Gt (19.16 t/cap), California 435,842,071 t, Wyoming 114,281,552 t, London ghs-fua_5288 67,630,310 t.

CORRECTION 1 (important): the v6 vs v7 gap is a scope difference, not a version discrepancy.
- v7 /rankings/countries with sectors=forestry-and-land-use returns −3,375,236,620 t for 2025.
- v7 with every sector except forestry-and-land-use returns 57,793,624,727 t, which exactly equals the v6 /country/emissions total (57,793,624,726.5).
- So v7 defaults include net forestry and land-use removals, while v6 excluded them.
- California's 435.8 Mt includes −18.8 Mt net forestry; without forestry it is about 454.6 Mt.
- Every Climate TRACE number needs a 'net incl. forestry/land use' or 'excl. LULUCF' scope chip. EDGAR's 54.1 Gt (excl. LULUCF) must never be compared side by side with Climate TRACE's 54.4 Gt (incl. net LULUCF). Like-for-like, Climate TRACE is 57.8 Gt excl. LULUCF.

CORRECTION 2: city IDs come from 'the GHS FUA dataset' (Functional Urban Areas), per the openapi field descriptions. They are not from GHS-UCDB R2024A (see the GHSL entry).

Use it for NDC and net-zero targets ('what has my government promised'), not for emissions republishing.
